15import logging 

16 

17import torch 

18 

19logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) 

20 

21# GCU400 has no SparseCOO TensorImpl, and aten's sparse COO constructor is not registered for 

22# SparsePrivateUse1, so tests of sparse metadata operators raise NotImplementedError while building inputs. 

23# This adds a CPU-side constructor: metadata queries do not read storage, so indices/values are copied to CPU 

24# to build an equivalent COO tensor with sparse_dim / dense_dim / shape / coalesced unchanged. 

25# Registration is idempotent and reusable by _dimV and similar operators. 

26_SPARSE_COO_FALLBACK_FLAG = "_flag_gems_gcu400_sparse_coo_fallback_registered" 

27_SPARSE_COO_LIBRARY = None 

28 

29 

30def _dimI(self: torch.Tensor) -> int: 

31 """Return the number of sparse dimensions of a sparse COO tensor ``self``. 

32 

33 Mirrors ``aten::_dimI(Tensor self) -> int``. This is a pure layout-metadata 

34 query: the answer is a property of the tensor's index layout, never of the 

35 stored element data, so there is no data movement and no Triton kernel. 

36 The result is read from TensorImpl/sparse-COO metadata without 

37 re-dispatching the ``_dimI`` operator itself (re-entering the dispatcher 

38 from inside a kernel registered on the Sparse dispatch key would recurse 

39 into this implementation). 

40 

41 Semantics by layout (verified against native ATen on H20, torch 

42 2.9.0+cu128): 

43 - ``torch.sparse_coo``: ``_dimI`` is the sparse dimension count, i.e. the 

44 leading dimension of the index matrix, ``self._indices().shape[0]`` 

45 (the native COO TensorImpl keeps the index matrix at shape 

46 ``(sparse_dim, nnz)``, so this equals ``self.sparse_dim()``). Plain 2-D 

47 COO gives 2, fully sparse rank-N COO gives N, and hybrid COO tensors 

48 (values carrying trailing dense dimensions) give the number of sparse 

49 dims only. Zero-nnz and uncoalesced tensors report the same value as 

50 their coalesced counterparts, because coalescing state does not change 

51 the layout. 

52 - Every other layout: native ATen registers ``aten::_dimI`` only for the 

53 Sparse (COO) backends -- strided, CSR/CSC (and BSR/BSC) raise 

54 ``NotImplementedError`` ("Could not run 'aten::_dimI' ... from the 

55 'CUDA'/'SparseCsrCUDA' backend"). Mirror that contract here instead of 

56 guessing a formula. 

57 logger.debug("GEMS_ENFLAME _DIMI") 

58 

59 Host-path notes (gcu400 hot-body form; do not regress): 

60 - The gate is ``self.is_sparse`` (ATen defines it as ``layout() == 

61 kSparse``), so it accepts exactly the COO layout and every other layout 

62 keeps raising, identical to a ``self.layout is torch.sparse_coo`` gate; 

63 it reads the cached bool straight from TensorImpl and is a few ns 

64 cheaper per call than the bound-layout enum comparison. 

65 - ``_indices().shape[0]`` is already a plain Python int, so no ``int()`` 

66 wrapper is needed. ``self.sparse_dim()`` is NOT used here: this backend 

67 registers a SparseCPU Python trampoline for it (~1.6us/call), while 

68 ``aten::_indices`` has no such trampoline and stays a native read. 

69 - There is deliberately no per-call ``logger.debug`` trace line: this 

70 op's whole cost is host-side metadata access (~0.2us) and a disabled 

71 debug call would be its single largest component (dense_dim/dimV/dim 

72 precedent on the enflame side). 

73 """ 

74 if self.is_sparse: 

75 return self._indices().shape[0] 

76 raise NotImplementedError( 

77 f"Could not run 'aten::_dimI' with arguments from the '{self.layout}' " 

78 "layout; aten::_dimI is only registered for the Sparse (COO) backends" 

79 )
